title: Climate-Responsive Data Centre Envelope Performance Under Contrasting Nepalese Climates
content: Data-centre cooling demand is dominated by continuous internal information technology (IT) heat generation, yet the effectiveness of envelope strategies across contrasting climates and IT-load intensities remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates twelve envelope and architectural scenarios for a 300 m² data-centre prototype under three contrasting climates using OpenStudio and EnergyPlus, complemented by IT-load sensitivity analysis and independent one-dimensional transient heat-transfer cross-verification. At 500 W/m², the combined reflective roof-and-wall case achieved annual cooling-demand reductions of 2.70–4.72%, while the passive radiative cooling-air-layer configuration produced the largest peak reductions of 7.20–11.57%. Insulation performance varied markedly with climate, and annual cooling demand increased under some cooler conditions. As IT-load density increased, relative envelope savings declined, whereas absolute annual savings remained comparatively stable. The findings show that data-centre envelope performance should be evaluated by considering the combined effects of climate, internal heat intensity, and annual versus peak cooling objectives to support climate-responsive and performance-based envelope design.
